result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Both answers cover the type order, pairing Devanagari with Latin, optical size and line-height adjustments, tabular Western digits, and print and phone proofing. B is more accurate about the A3-to-phone problem. It works out that the page shrinks to about 22% and recommends a separate phone layout. A claims that text at 28pt or above stays readable, which is wrong. B also adds useful PDF checks: tagging, language marking, live text and contrast. Neither answer clearly says that a Latin-only font will produce missing glyphs or a silent fallback for Hindi. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): Both answers are strong. They both give tabular Western digits in both scripts, larger size and line height for Devanagari, and proof checks on the print and the phone. B gives a clearer size and weight table for the order of roles, and it comes closer to warning that a Latin face can't supply Devanagari glyphs and would lead to substitution. A is better on the phone layout, but it never says plainly that a Latin-only font won't render Hindi.
